summary: This substantial finite-lattice manuscript appears mathematically coherent on complete analytical reading. Its strongest contributions are constructive target-order rectangular observations under partial coordinate invariance, carefully scoped comparison obstructions, and local shell bounds with sharp moment/thickness limitations. No principal theorem-invalidating objection was identified. Classical mechanisms and unfinished priority comparison limit originality and broader importance. Minor revisions should consolidate contributions, dependencies and direct immutable evidence links. All 88 pages were read as text and on contact sheets; 18 individual full-page images were inspected. No formal or scientific execution, independence or human peer review is claimed.
strengths: Constructs actual finite Fourier/coexact spaces and observations with explicit normalization and quantifier discipline.
The partial-coordinate invariance theorem gives target-order disjoint rectangular means with K=c, including odd sizes and singleton cells.
The shell section proves both inverse-moment endpoints from actual internal energy and supplies a starting-site sharpness family.
Separates failed sufficient certificates from failed observation problems and often supplies successful observations on the same examples.
Handles singular Schur compatibility, constant-mode penalty floors and actual physical/coexact embeddings explicitly.
weaknesses: Priority of the precise restricted constructions and shell formulation remains unestablished despite useful classical attribution.
The unrestricted fully variable critical rectangular problem and interacting/continuum applications remain open.
The 88-page accumulation and repeated provenance narrative make contribution and dependency structure difficult to navigate.
Historical formal execution and diagnostic provenance were not authenticated in this review.
No sharp minimum rank, stable implementation, efficient runtime or demonstrated external reuse is established.
potential_errors: No demonstrated error in a principal mathematical claim was found; this analytical AI review is not a proof certification.
Transferring spectral rank to rectangular means, or kernel coercivity to the same penalty coefficient, would be invalid without the retained extra hypotheses.
The lower shell moment estimate requires its thickness cost and does not provide a disjoint partition or preserve the global critical moment in its sharpness examples.
Statements about historical builds, source audits, archives and runtimes remain manuscript assertions rather than verified results of this review.
